hypothesis: Longest-processing-time-first launch order for causal prefill: reorder the _attn_fwd grid to (H, num_m_blocks, B) so query heads vary fastest, and map program_id(1) to start_m = num_m_blocks - 1 - pid1 when CAUSAL. All heads' heaviest (bottom-of-triangle) m-blocks launch first and the cheapest diagonal-only blocks fill the tail; non-causal keeps natural m order.
rationale: Prefill rows are the thinnest margin over FA2 (1.01-1.03x; prefill_2048 ~1.01x). With causal block skipping, m-block work is linear in start_m, but the current grid launches m-blocks in ascending order per head (light first, heavy last), so the final wave is dominated by the most expensive blocks and SMs idle at the end (prefill_2048 at BLOCK_M 128 is only ~3 waves of 1 block/SM over 170 SMs). Global heavy-first ordering is the classic LPT fix (FA2/FA3 also schedule causal blocks in reverse). Heads-fastest also puts the GROUP=4 q-heads sharing a KV head into adjacent CTAs that stream the same K/V tiles in lockstep, keeping L2 reuse; reuse distance at 32k stays well under 96 MiB L2. Not tried before (noted as 'next' in exps 2-5).
expected_effect: Small-to-moderate prefill gain from shorter tail, largest on prefill_2048/4096 (few waves), roughly neutral on 16k/32k; decode untouched (split path).
